title: Data Types [char]
description:
## char
A `char` in Rust represents a single character. Unlike strings, chars use single quotes.
```rust
let c: char = 'A';
let digit: char = '7';
let emoji: char = '🦀';
```
Rust chars are 4 bytes and support full Unicode - so yes, even emojis.
## Printing vars.
To print a var in rust, in the printed string you put `{}` and then pass another argument, the variable, such as `println!("thing = {}", thing);`
